A full 512-state enumeration for each graph and an independent vertex-subset connectivity recurrence agree as polynomial distributions. Their exactly factored tail differences are positive for every 0<p<1. Tail-sum moment identities yield the displayed degree-12 Q(p), and the u=p/(1-p) transform has precisely one coefficient sign change, proving one simple interior root using the opposite endpoint signs. The proof covers the continuum analytically; a numerical grid is not substituted for proof.

value.rationale: This is the smallest possible nontrivial comparison of connected simple cubic contact networks, controlling network size and vertex degree while varying only triangle structure. The exact strict stochastic ordering coexists with a reversed variance ordering above an explicit unique threshold. This resolves the natural question whether better outbreak spread in this first regular-graph pair also entails greater dispersion; the answer is no. The precise root and full tail-factorization make it a benchmark for finite epidemic risk and stochastic-order-vs-variance distinction, beyond mere coefficient tabulation.
